evals.prompt:
Review this Automation runbook for security problems before I share it with other teams, and give me a hardened version:

```yaml
schemaVersion: '0.3'
description: Restarts the app service and rotates its log directory.
assumeRole: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/AppOpsRole
parameters:
  InstanceId:
    type: String
  LogPath:
    type: String
    allowedPattern: '.*'
  DbPassword:
    type: SecureString
mainSteps:
  - name: RotateLogs
    action: aws:runCommand
    onFailure: Continue
    inputs:
      DocumentName: AWS-RunShellScript
      InstanceIds: ['{{InstanceId}}']
      Parameters:
        commands:
          - tar czf /var/tmp/logs.tgz {{LogPath}} && rm -rf {{LogPath}}/*
          - echo "restarting with password {{DbPassword}}"
          - curl -k https://internal-api.example.com/notify
  - name: CheckHealth
    action: aws:executeScript
    timeoutSeconds: 1200
    onCancel: step:Wait
    inputs:
      Runtime: python3.11
      Handler: handler
      Script: |-
        import boto3
        def handler(events, context):
            return boto3.client('ec2').describe_instance_status()
  - name: Wait
    action: aws:sleep
    inputs: {Duration: PT10S}
```
evals.expected_output: Reports: command injection through LogPath in the runCommand commands with a weak '.*' pattern (critical); DbPassword declared as SecureString, which isn't a valid document parameter type, and echoed in a command (critical, without repeating any value); missing allowedPattern on InstanceId; curl -k disabling TLS verification; a hard-coded assumeRole ARN instead of {{AutomationAssumeRole}}; timeoutSeconds 1200 above the 600-second aws:executeScript maximum; onCancel routed to an aws:sleep step, which isn't a valid cancel target; and lists onFailure: Continue on RotateLogs as information. Returns a hardened YAML document with an anchored LogPath pattern, the instance ID pattern, a Parameter Store name parameter read at run time, the -k flag removed, assumeRole parameterised, the timeout lowered to 600 and onCancel fixed, each change cited.
assertions: Flags LogPath as a command-injection risk because its pattern is '.*' and it is interpolated into a shell command
Flags SecureString as an invalid parameter type and recommends taking the Parameter Store parameter name instead
Flags the echo of DbPassword as exposing a secret
Flags curl -k as disabling TLS verification
Flags the hard-coded assumeRole ARN
Flags timeoutSeconds 1200 as above the aws:executeScript maximum of 600 seconds
Flags onCancel routing to an aws:sleep step as invalid
Returns a complete hardened document in YAML
Cites a documentation page for findings

assertions.text: The instance ID pattern is applied
The executeScript timeout is lowered to 600
No raw 12-digit account ID other than the documentation example is exposed

evals.prompt:
Check this runbook before release:

```yaml
schemaVersion: '0.3'
description: Stops an EC2 instance.
assumeRole: '{{AutomationAssumeRole}}'
parameters:
  AutomationAssumeRole:
    type: AWS::IAM::Role::Arn
  InstanceId:
    type: String
    allowedPattern: '^i-(?:[a-f0-9]{8}|[a-f0-9]{17})$'
  KeyName:
    type: String
    allowedPattern: '^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,255}$'
mainSteps:
  - name: StopInstance
    action: aws:changeInstanceState
    inputs:
      InstanceIds: ['{{InstanceId}}']
      DesiredState: stopped
```
evals.expected_output: Reports no critical or high findings. Does not treat KeyName as a secret parameter, does not ask for a timeoutSeconds on aws:changeInstanceState, and returns the document unchanged or with only optional low-severity notes.
assertions: Reports no critical or high findings
Does not flag KeyName as a secret
Does not require timeoutSeconds on the aws:changeInstanceState step
